question: Does a data-scaled (4,800-task) imitation constructor beat streaming enumeration on solves at equal total CPU at a declared volume of 12,000 tasks on a shape-broad bank?
scope_note: Shape-broad sampling: complete levels 6/7; level 8 balanced across left-subtree sizes; exclusions: v1 corpus, sealed hard corpus, and all D1/D2 dev identities; any shortfall is recorded, never silently rebalanced.

data.final_split_access: Do not run model inference on eval tasks until this fixture carries corpus_sha256 and frozen_at.

evaluation.failure_policy: Retain failures, premature stops, budget exhaustion and invalid actions.

decision_rules.kill_criterion: if the data-scaled learned arm does not beat streaming on solves at equal total CPU (fit charged, truncated at the common budget, declared volume 12,000) on the sealed shape-broad bank, the data-scaling route closes at accessible scale — no retest at larger volume, wider beam, or larger train pool.
